title: Tenant caged scheduling and granular QoS policy for GPU lanes
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant ‘caged scheduling’ mode plus a configurable granular QoS policy that enforces per-tenant throughput guarantees, progressive soft-throttles, and deterministic eviction windows for noisy-neighbor mitigation on Dedicated GPU lanes. Scope includes scheduler changes (lane fencing), quota enforcement API, autoscale hook integration, and Console controls + observability.

Motivation: Several pilot customers reported tail-latency spikes during multi-tenant bursts and observed variable throughput despite committed capacity. Current token-based soft quotas cannot express per-tenant minimum throughput guarantees or progressive degradation behavior for long-running batch workloads.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- Approach: Introduce 'caged' lanes concept: a logical reservation slice that guarantees a minimum tensor-throughput (tokens/s) per tenant while allowing burst headroom. Implement a QoS policy engine that maps SLA classes -> token/bandwidth reservations + eviction priority.
- Tradeoffs: Stronger guarantees increase fragmentation and reduce overall utilization. To mitigate, we will implement predictive spillover (best-effort bursting) and a cooperative reclaim window to allow short bursts across cages.
- Kernel-level changes: no new kernels required; scheduler will coordinate KV-cache placement and preferential batching to honor throughput windows.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Per-tenant baseline throughput guarantee (configurable) can be set via API/Console and is enforced under 95th percentile load tests.
2) Noisy neighbor events produce deterministic soft degrade behavior (latency SLOs degrade gracefully) and clear audit logs.
3) Autoscale hooks can opt-in to tie lane resizing to vacancy signals without violating guarantees.
4) Console shows token-level and lane-level SLO dashboards, and a 'cage health' indicator.

Open design docs / links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DEDICATED/Tenant+Caged+Scheduling+Design
- Prototype scheduler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
- Load test dashboards (internal): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/lanes/tenant-cage-load-tests

Implementation plan: 3 phases across 4 sprints.
- Phase 1 (this ticket): Scheduler primitives, quota API, basic Console toggles, and unit tests.
- Phase 2: Eviction scoring, predictive spillover, KV-cache affinity, integration tests and canary rollout to non-production Dedicated clusters.
- Phase 3: Customer rollouts, full observability, and policy-based autoscale tuning.

Monitoring & SLOs: Add new SLOs: tenant-throughput-guard (p99 >= configured guarantee), cage-eviction-rate (<0.5% under steady state), noisy-neighbor-alerts (count). Alert playbook will wire into on-call runbook.

Rollout plan: Canary on two non-production Dedicated regions -> staged ramp to 10% of Dedicated production lanes (week-by-week) -> customer opt-in per tenancy.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-fragmentation reduces cluster utilization -> Mitigation: predictive spillover and periodic rebalancer that transparently redistributes cages overnight.
- Risk: Mis-configured guarantees create SLA mismatch -> Mitigation: Console warns when requested guarantees exceed physical capacity and provides simulated impact.

Next steps:
- Deliver initial scheduler PR and run 48h soak using benchmark harness (assigned to @dpark). PR link in 'updates' below.

Test plan: unit + e2e in CI, synthetic tail-burst scenarios, long-run soak (72h) with mixed bursty/batch tenants, and customer pilot with monitoring export to their dashboards.

2026-02-24: Prototype PR opened (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821). Initial benchmark shows 18% drop in max cluster utilization but 85% reduction in tail-latency variance for guarded tenants.
2026-03-02: Design review with SRE and Product; decision to make predictive spillover opt-in per cage to preserve hard guarantees by default. Added console warning for high-guarantee requests.
2026-03-08: Integration tests added to CI (tenant-cage e2e). Found KV-cache affinity edge cases when cages migrate; created follow-up ENG-521433 to address migration KV-cache rebind handshake.
